item.title: South Africa, time to change the guards.
item.dc:creator: davidrobertlewis
item.content:encoded: South Africa needs a change of government. After 15 years of ANC rule it is time for the party to join the ranks of the opposition. Is it because the ANC no longer represents the genuine aspirations of the people of South Africa, the majority of whom believe in human rights, freedom and equality for all? Is it because the ANC youth league is headed by a black supremacist and race chauvinist, while the Zuma administration continues to espouse the politics of race-hatred via race-based capitalism -- an ideological framework which has begun to resemble the dirty tricks of the apartheid-era National Party government. Our government is nothing less than a corrupt political force which serves no other purpose than to line the pockets of a small power elite via the hypocritical deployment of "Socialism for the Few" before the brainwashed masses while hanging on to the racial categories defined by the apartheid regime. Strip away the Orwellian double-speak of doing one thing and saying another, and the only language spoken by the ANC is the language of power and corruption. You can see it in the smoke and mirrors charade of Polakwane. The constant weaving this way and that on a variety of issues, with a final resort to tribalism and ethnicity in order to garner votes while covering up the truth of the many deals which go far beyond negotiated compromises to seriously jeopardizing the right of any ANC member to rule this country within the bounds of law. The contradictions within the party are now so apparent that anybody who considers themselves a member does so only because they have given up the idea of social justice and have embraced the contradictions. Take the fact that both Maria Ramos and ex-Minister Valli Moosa (now head of the neo-conservative World Conservation Union) sit on the same board of directors as apartheid supremo Boetie Van Zyl -- Sanlam is the de facto holding company of Naspers/Media24, -- or that the final report of the TRC has been resoundingly trashed by senior counsel acting on their behalf? Five months ago I appeared in the Labour Court of Cape Town, facing a barrage of attacks from lawyers appearing on behalf of Media24. The attacks were informed by apartheid and raised the spectre of South Africa’s racial classification system. Not only has the corporation insisted that I belong to a particular racial category but Media24 continues to maintain that legal consequences should be attached to issues of race and that my own characterization of my skin colour as “coloured” is both “wrong” and “ridiculous”. I am now in the process of formulating criminal charges against the corporation for perpetuating and perpetrating a gross violation and crime against humanity by asserting both race and a racial classification system. If we define apartheid in its most basic terms, it is the delineation of citizenship along racial lines. Such blatant racism in a court of law is surely illegal in our day and age, and yet Naspers believes it may act with impunity, because its boardroom resembles a whose who of international finance and banking. Another sad reality is Media24 has also demanded that Jews register in order to receive Labour rights and/or that the court make a ruling which would achieve a similar effect as forcing staff of Jewish descent to wear yellow stars. The corporation has also persisted in downplaying and undermining the role of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) disparaging both its findings and impugning the dignity of the victims of apartheid, many of whom made submissions to the commission. The evidence and argument lead by myself in papers before the court has furthermore been mischaracterised by the company as a “denial of reality”. Yet Media24 choose to look the other way, maintaining that apartheid has been “dismantled long ago” but at the same time refusing to accept any of the findings made by the commission, (or that the finding constitutes evidence in a court of law). They are not alone. The ANC ruling party has also failed to make good on any of the TRC recommendations. In effect, under the present regime, there is no possibility of the truth -- There can be no criticism and dissent at the company as far as senior counsel are concerned, and it would appear that the issue has been removed a priori, in the form of a series of deals made between the corporation and the ANC ruling party. (Please see the fact-sheet below) ANC tycoons and party oligarchs have sold out our most basic human rights, installing a few individuals into positions of power while denying calls for restitution and justice. Corruption knows no bounds as the court fails to deliver its verdict for the sixth successive month. We have all been duped into believing that justice and reconciliation in the new South Africa is possible. Media24 continue to claim expert knowledge of the legal framework set in motion by the TRC, knowing full well they have been allowed to escape without being forced to face questioning on their role during apartheid, and despite being condemned for directly supporting the racist regime. They will stoop to any level to achieve their goal, to escape history (and justice) to the point of denying that apartheid ever existed. With regard to Media24 non-compliance with the TRC, in papers before the court, the court was subjected to pleas for “absolution from the instance” and a multitude of obfuscations, errors and falsehoods: C Kahanowitz SC expressed the prevailing culture at the company, by scoffing at the implications: “The only way, or so it was argued, that this “chain of shame” could ever be broken, was through the ritual purging of the corporation via the TRC.” This merely demonstrates the way the truth makes way for lies of the worst kind — Media24 has become nothing more than the propaganda wing of the puppet government behind the ANC alliance, as we all fall prey to the parallel reality created by a failure to uphold the TRC. A circular published by the Broederbond states: “The Afrikanerdom shall reach its ultimate destiny of domination in South Africa . . . Brothers, our solution for South Africa?s troubles is not that this or that party shall gain the upper hand, but that the Afrikaner Broederbond shall rule South Africa.” Was the TRC a mere ritual? Is the final report of no consequence? Media24 (and the ANC) have been exposed as liars, who were not only condemned by the commission, but are now seriously adrift from the truth. They have frauded, and continue to defraud innocent South Africans, and yet the justice department overlooks their crimes while media executives are rewarded with bonuses. Naspers recently posted a 21% increase in profits. Media24 are still unable to supply a bone fide contract of employment and a fraud docket case 188/2010 has been opened in connection with the fraudulent attachment of my signature to a legal document, presented as evidence in the case. An employee who testified on the company’s behalf was unable to corroborate the corporation’s “official version of events” and contradicted her own testimony on a multitude of occasions. The company has also manufactured a badly constructed and pathetic story to explain how I came to be dismissed without reference to the Labour Relations Act (LRA) The sad counter-accusations of plagiarism by Media24 in connection to a contentious music industry story have been slammed by senior lecturers in the Department of Journalism at University of Witwatersrand, as having no basis in fact. I have email correspondence from Lesley Cowling who says: “You clearly attribute the information you took from the website and put it in quotes.” How dare I quote an online biography in a world in which the Internet is a ubiquitous source of information? How dare I quote a website not owned by the company? In papers before the court it was shown that Dean had not bothered to follow guidelines laid down by the company for investigation into her outrageous claim that I fabricated a news story and concocted an interview with a well-known Jazz musician, the company still insists that its version of events is both true and accurate. The Labour Court also heard deliberation on whether or not I had given Media24 the number of Mr Jansen and the company was forced to concede that I had indeed given an editor the number of Pastor Glen Robertson via which Jansen could be contacted. (Mr Jansen is currently in ICU fighting for his life!!) I have categorically stated that if the views or opinions of Robbie Jansen can be construed as being political then I am too of the same opinion. Annelien Dean, editor of People’s Post on the other hand continues to maintain that an interview with Mr Jansen was as she put it “borderline plagiarism” and “too controversial” to publish, while the company asserted that the views of Mr Jansen were “music industry politics”. Sheer racism as far as I am concerned. How long must I wait for the Labour court to decide whether or not I am a human being, and whether it is okay to listen to Jazz at a mixed race venue? Why should there be any legal consequences attached to race or skin complexion in our age? Why are we still banning Jazz musicians and suffering behind the walls of segregation, forced to live in the shadow of the National Party (ANC) and its official lies? Down with this brutal censorship by these Naspers/National (ANC) party cronies. One would think that given the weight of public and international opinion, that Media24 would throw in the towel, but instead they persist with their strange belief that only they have access to the truth, manipulating and abusing their position of power created by an alliance with ANC corporate stooges. Media24 have on a number of occasions also threatened to gag me and have attempted to bring a counter defamation suite in 2006, which failed. A pamphlet endorsed by the Social Movements Indaba, in support of my case, states: “A former struggle journalist was thrown out of a community newsroom for writing an article about a well-known jazz musician and attending a mixed Jazz venue on a Friday night.” Considering the outrageous circumstance’s (there is also an issue of overtime) I have asked the court to uphold the rights of Jews (to dissent) in relation to the Jewish Sabbath which occurs on a Friday night, (what I do on the Sabbath is between me and my Sabbath) and have lead expert testimony on the matter and manner in which Media24 have flagrantly disregarded my rights as a Jew (and struggle journalist) to freely associate and to make use of the Sabbath as I see fit. In retaliation, the company has accused me of being a “fake Jew” and cynically abusing the faith of others. They have also accused me of concocting a "feeble attempt to bolster my case" since I am "not a coloured but a white male," thereby asserting, in writing a fact of law which is clearly unscientific and without foundation. Our constitution upholds the right to freedom of thought, belief and opinion, and I have every right to contest my apartheid-era birth certificate accordingly. This is not a case about the Sabbath per se, nor is it about who is or who is not a Jew -- who is black or who is white -- it is a case about the failure of a racist media company to renew a contract of employment for a prohibited reason, this reason being discrimination for a listed reason. Whatever the outcome, I believe I have shown the court the manner in which differentiation in terms of Media24 news room policy informed as it was by the apartheid system which continues until this day, and sanctioned by the ANC government resulted in disparate treatment as an individual, and any court should make a similar finding accordingly.

item.title: Why I no longer believe in Mandela
item.dc:creator: davidrobertlewis
item.content:encoded:
Mandela the Myth informed my childhood. Like many South Africans of the 80s generation, I grew up in a State of Emergency. Political parties to the left were banned and Mandela was imprisoned on Robben Island. Although the slogan: Free Mandela, was synonymous with the liberation struggle, it was the Freedom Charter which inspired us. Pitted against a white minority regime which had literally succeeded in erasing Mandela's identity -- no contemporary photographs of Mandela existed --  attempts to read Mandela's writing were met with official statements about the possession of banned material -- one activist was imprisoned merely for having a tattoo with the the words Free Mandela. Like the black consciousness leader Biko, songs about Mandela could get you into serious trouble with the National Party regime. When Mandela was finally released and the press could photograph him, we waited with thousands of our fellow compatriots for hours on Cape Town's Grand Parade, to catch a glimpse of the living legend. The slow transition to democracy was not without its pitfalls. The CODESA negotiations between the National Party and the ANC often broke down under threat of far right wing elements taking up arms, while political structures began to merge in the expectation of freedom -- the line separating authority,  the security forces from those on the other side in the anti-apartheid movement, rapidly blurring, and to a frightening degree. The result was a short period spent in self-inflicted exile, I left my homeland, South Africa following the assassination of communist party leader Chris Hani. Upon returning, I had been given the grace to attend a triumphant "Artists Against Apartheid" exhibition, held in our very first democratically elected Parliament -- only to be  amazed as  South Africa's first black President, Nelson Mandela emerged, a veritable 12 foot giant* whose very presence spoke of freedom. The Velvet Revolution began during the Cape Town Peace March turned into the Champagne Revolution. Eventually the effervescence of the transition wore off. Gradually life returned to normal.  We slowly stopped believing in Nelson Mandela the legend, as it became clear that he was all too human and fallible. A simple politician more interested in the art of the grand gesture, than the finer details of freedom. Mandela, it appeared, always on the lookout for an opportunity to showcase his trademark colourful shirts, would rather visit the widow of the late Hendrik Verwoerd to placate the right-wing, than actively promote the substance of the Freedom Charter by visiting ordinary people in the townships. Although South Africa, which had gotten over the euphoric Mandela presidency by this stage,  had a new constitution supposedly guaranteeing equal rights, freedom of thought, opinion and religion,  it soon became a sin in my own country to even dare to criticise Mandela's many failures.  His silence on Israel and Palestine. His uncomfortable prevarication on Myanmar and Tibet. The truth is, Mandela never stood up for human rights in the way we all wanted him to be a superman activist, dealing with every possible problem under the sun. Rather he stood up, in a humble way for his own troubles. The result?  A political party which has now constituted itself as some form of mass religion, "more popular than even Jesus Christ" in the process encouraging a personality cult which insists upon the infallibility of leadership, the unquestioning virtue of "Brand Madiba" which grants succor to  all  political cronies who have ascended the throne after him. [caption id="attachment_5085" align="alignleft" width="300"] Golden Handshake for Mandela's warden while "white left" shafted by BEE.[/caption] An astute politician, of that there can be no doubt. But an infallible demigod, whose every word is the truth? Mandela, for all his post-1994 writing, produced few great speeches. Many of his aphorisms and quotable quotes were written by other people, in particular his biographers. He generously accepted the position we, the people, vested upon him, living up to his historical role as a South African liberator, but he never stood up for universal human rights in later life, in the way Gandhi, or Martin Luther King stood up, regardless of who the recipients might be and in what nation they might reside. The criticism, mostly unpopular, that Mandela advocated violence and refused to condemn aggression when it was unleashed, continues.  Mandela however, managed to break with his party on support for the Treatment Action Campaign while remaining quiet on other issues, such as the arms scandal, for which the ANC deserved to be condemned. History will judge Mandela thus as a creation of the 20th century. A scion of MTV sound-bytes, and race identity cliché. A media concoction which produced a peculiar one dimensional world of black and white, in which the lives of ordinary people, in particular the working class, came a distant second. Mandela upon his 2012 birthday, is now a retired and silenced leader of a country which has failed to deliver on its promise of human rights for all. The majority of South Africans still live in poverty, while a paternalistic state makes mince meat of the principles for which he rightly or wrongly, appears to have taken all the credit. If Mandela was really the great statesman and jurist he (and his supporters) so claim him to be, then why is it that South Africa has a corrupt judiciary that maintains the last vestiges of apartheid? The idea that the small legal practice of Mandela and Sisulu would lead to greater things has proven false. Is there nothing universal about the Freedom Struggle? How is it possible that our nation's judges continue to disavow internationally accepted best practice, while maintaining they, and only they,  are entitled to declaim on the rights of citizens without citizens being afforded equality before the law? It is uncomfortable questions such as these, which in the final analysis show up Mandela as all too human. A failed superhero whose legacy will only come to fruition once we have truly liberated our people.
  • * Note: Mr Mandela's height was 6ft 4ins (1.93 metres)
SEE: Towards a reappraisal of Mandela & No, Malaika, you weren't liberated by Mandela

item.title: Apartheid denial, an emerging industry
item.dc:creator: davidrobertlewis
item.content:encoded: There are no departments dedicated to "psychohistory" in any institution of higher learning, some history departments have run courses in it and a new field of study known as "cliodynamics" which has taken over the fields of interest formally associated with psychohistory. Still, psychohistory remains a controversial field of study, facing criticism in the academic community,with critics referring to it as a pseudoscience.Psychohistory uses a plurality of methodologies, and it is difficult to determine which is appropriate to use in each circumstance. DeMause has received criticism on several levels. His formulations have been criticized for being insufficiently supported by credible research. He has also received criticism for being a strong proponent of the "black legend" view of childhood history (i.e. that the history of childhood was above all a history of progress, with children being far more often badly mistreated in the past). Similarly, his work has been called a history of child abuse, not childhood. “Ask a historian in mid-career to reminisce about the heyday of psychohistory and you are likely to see him (or, more rarely, her) step out of his detached, professional role. He will struggle manfully to suppress a grimqace that is familier to anyone who has watched a member of the baby boom generation confronted with a slogan-covered button from the attic or a college paperback complete with compromising marginalia. Rightly or wrongly, today’s feelings about psychohistory overlap with feelings about the sixties so that the two are difficult to untangle. True believers in the ethos of the decade emergeged from it s embittered, unrepentant, or still embattled. Those who opposed that ethos watched in triumph or relief as it was abandoned, sometimes mixed with chagrin at what has replaced it.” James Walkup, Why is most Psychohistory So Bad? SouthWest Review, Vol 73 no 3 Summer 1988

item.title: Heart of Kakness Part II
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
I had just been fired, the very same day I had scheduled a lunch-time interview with poet Gabeeba Badaroon, a sequal to my piece on Rustum Kozain. There I sat in Athlone at a well-known Cafe, still shaken from the events which had transpired.

She cut a sightly figure, slender and good-looking, a hint of the exotic about her, that clearly spoke through her poetry which I found absolutely fascinating, yet instead of proceeding, we just sat there, she could tell that something was wrong. I said, 'look I've just been fired, so there's no point to this interview.'

She spoke about Tagore and Pablo Naruda, I scribbled some notes and we parted.

My ride was a converted delivery bike, but the would-be cafe racer decided to get a flat, forcing me to abandon it in Athlone, and I just walked and walked, until I got to Observatory, arriving just in time for an art exhibition.

The wine flowed as it usually does at such events, and so I foolishly called Dean on my mobile, just to tell her that I had met with Gabeeba, was now at an awesome artist event and that she should remember exactly what I said today.

My exact words never came up in the case that would take four years to get on the Labour Court roll, instead a bastardised version, wholly concocted from the imagination passed for the testimony that would take precedence over my own.

If there had been any hint at the anti-Semitism which was to come, it was a well-kept secret, since I also foolishly believed the South African Constitution and its promise of a non-racial society in which every man, woman and child, would be guaranteed rights and freedoms.

Little did I know that our legal system was stubbornly refusing to enter the new country or that with its feet fixed in the past, its modus was to feed the exact same party political hustle and corruption that had previously kept the Nationalists in power.

It was thus as a relative novice that I approached my legal insurer, seeking to gain the rest of my salary, and seeking advice on the matter at hand. It was nearly Autumn, my only previous engagement with the legal system as such had been a brief detention for putting up posters whilst at UCT.

Though Caledon Square was covered with the rotten stench of blood, and its cells had been scrawled with the words of prisoners taken in by Botha, Malan and Vlok, the system had perhaps, been too kind to me, and I had been, let off with just a fine.

Back in the new country of Mandela and Mbeki, an arbitration of a dispute involving the Independent Group some five years previously had been settled out of court, and a claim made via the Small Claims Court in my favour had been duly paid over by the company.

It was now that I requested sight of my salary in terms of the contract, and advised Media24 that I was NOT an Orthodox Jew, but in any event, 'Jews celebrated the Sabbath from 'Friday sunset to Saturday sunset'.

The result was that some weeks later I received a lump sum payment constituting the remaining months salary and including a bit of overtime.

A 'receipt of payment' drafted by Legalwise and thus a 'settlement' marked Without Prejudice was duly signed. As to what to do next, as Winter approached they were woefully silent.

I therefore hastened to open a complaint at the Human Rights Commission on my own steam, at the same time I filled out an obligatory CCMA form, in regard to a labour dispute involving an unfair policy or practice, namely racism. It would take the SAHRC the entire Winter to respond and when they did, they passed the buck, citing the incorrect fact that the matter was now already before the Labour Court.

Needless to say, the CCMA matter proceeded, without the other parties appearance. As the Human Rights Commission had already indicated, the matter was then referred to the Labour Court.

At first my insurer appeared to take up the cudgels once again, but then balked. The reason was bound up with events which transpired at the inaugural Cape Town Book Fair. An event which had been publicised to the press in the very weeks that I started working in Bellville. It was also bound up with the manner in which a series of similar events such as a History of Slavery IZIKO and an exhibition of Pre-Islamic Art at the Bo Kaap Museum, had been cut out from the so-called community newspapers.

I thus convened a meeting of a rag-tag group of activists at Community House to discuss the problem, created a platform called the Alternative Media Forum and released a pamphlet, which was flyered at the event, resulting in my gaining a dinner with Dennis Brutus, and George Hallet.

It was not at all shocking when I received a 'Cease and Desist' from Media24, and the resulting response from the Freedom of Expression Institute opposing the gagging.

Cape Law Society were even kind enough to appoint Abrahams and Gross to defend me, and thus Sarah Dodd took up the cudgels etc.

item.title: Read your critics, or die of starvation
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
IT IS NEVER easy to admit fault. Have we reached the point where we require a correction, an antidote to, too much leftism?

Being on the left field for for most of my life I must admit reading the Wikipedia page detailing criticism of socialism, alongside contributions by foremost critics from (Egad!), the Austrian school of economics such as Mises and Hayek, two theorists one should learn to love and hate, one is struck at how the page resembles a criticism of South Africa's economy.

Many of the critiques drafted during the 30s and 40s are readily applied to our situation, the problem of economic calculation inherent to state enterprises, inability to allocate resources, lack of technological innovation, and the suppression of economic democracy and self-management.

Those on the right of the spectrum are not alone. Central planning is also criticized by elements of the radical left. So too by Proudhon, whose own criticism of 'economic calculation' deserves reading.

Libertarian socialist economist Robin Hahnel notes that 'even if central planning overcame its inherent inhibitions of incentives and innovation, it would nevertheless be unable to maximize economic democracy and self-management, which he believes are concepts that are more intellectually coherent, consistent and just than mainstream notions of economic freedom.'

Centralisation results in reduced prosperity, reduced incentives and reduced innovation with its terrible outcome, leadership corruption. Ring any bells?

To show readers that I not about to throw my lot in with the Austrian School any time soon, I still advocate a co-ownership democracy, one in which a social wage plays an important part. I just no longer have any use for the doctrinaire socialist debates that were all the rage on campus during the 80s and 90s, nor the pathetic indictments of neoliberalism penned by collage graduate over the millennium, and still popping up, many of which are responsible for the economic meltdown we are experiencing in so many sectors.

Look, its not entirely the fault of Covid-19 or socialist bureaucrats from the World Health Organisation. South Africa's bureaucrats have created a state that is amped up on regulation, red-tape and a bloated public sector but with very little to show for the exercise.

Are we paying a high price for devaluing the individual and 'making people incapable of choosing their own values as decisions are made centrally." In essence, are we throttling the private sector whilst destroying the commons in favour of a state enterprise called Republic of SA?

You may be surprised to find that this criticism is central to those who follow the works of Ayan Rand. I guess another Egad is in order. Read your critics before you die of starvation is all I have to offer.

item.title: There is no "Gay Science"
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
On 29 August 2019 the largest study1 to date on the genetic basis of sexuality has revealed five spots on the human genome that are linked to same-sex sexual behaviour — but "none of the markers are reliable enough to predict someone’s sexuality". 

The research published in Science and based on the genomes of nearly 500,000 people, shore up the results of earlier, smaller studies and confirm the suspicions of many scientists: while sexual preferences have a genetic component, no single gene has a large effect on sexual behaviours.

“There is no ‘gay gene’,” says lead study author Andrea Ganna, a geneticist at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

item.title: Tritium found in groundwater outside Koeberg
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
INFORMATION released by environmental organisation Koeberg Alert Alliance, point to ongoing reactor design problems associated with normal operations at the plant. In particular the production of elemental Tritium (3H) and tritiated water (3H2O) during the course of nuclear fission. The organisation has previously drawn attention to Tritium releases and the resulting contamination of borehole water and the water table surrounding Koeberg, in submissions on the environmental impact of a previous project known as Nuclear 1.

"Tritium levels of <3 TU are the “norm” at the Koeberg site but elevated levels of 4.8, 5.5 and 42 TU have been recorded in three boreholes within 50 m of the plant buildings", according to a report by SRK Consulting conducted over a decade ago in 2010 and referred to by Koeberg Alert

The SRk report maintains: "These levels are the result of known releases of tritiated steam and condensate and the pathways are as per the original design of the plant and are not due to uncontrolled releases or leaks."

The report then concluded: "The presence of tritium in groundwater at these levels does not pose a risk to people or the environment" but failed to explain a contamination incident inside the plant affecting 91 workers at the time the report was drafted and in all likelihood the result of Tritium The claim of zero health impact is disputed by KAA.

According to the Nuclear Industry Association of South Africa (NIASA) "The greatest source of radioactivity in the reactor coolant circuit is, however, irradiation of the coolant itself. Neutron bombardment of nitrogen dissolved in the water gives rise to carbon-14. Moreover, irradiation of boron dissolved in the coolant water creates hydrogen-3, i.e. tritium, the radioactive isotope of hydrogen.”

"Radioisotopes such as cobalt-58, cobalt-60 and silver-110m arise as a result of wear or corrosion of reactor components. They become radioactive due to neutron bombardment as they circulate through the reactor with the primary circuit cooling water."

Both Tritium and Tritiated Water are sources of beta particle radiation. It is suspected that elemental Tritium is the more likely culprit behind the production of Cobalt-58 dust affecting the workers, who would not ordinarily come into contact with the primary coolant.

At the time Eskom spokeswoman Karen de Villiers claimed the exposures to radiation caused by exposure to the dust particles were low, "about 0.5 percent of the annually allowed exposure limit."

Co-58 has a half-life of 70.86 days, which is the 'approximate time required for a quantity to reduce to half of its initial value'. The substance is a source of beta and gamma radiation. It would thus take 70 days to become half as radioactive, another 70 days to become a quarter and so on, and is thus radioactive for months.

Elemental Tritium is able to diffuse through metals, particularly in the presence of heat, and is a direct consequence of fission, where production of Tritium occurs in about "one atom per 10,000 fissions" as a direct consequence of the fission process. Whereas Tritiated Water (HTO) is the result of neutron bombardment of water. Tritium has a half-life of 12 years, and a decay chain to Helium-3 (3H).

Although not considered chemically toxic, it is nevertheless a source of radiation, and impacts upon the longevity of the plant, which is nearings its design limits and is due for decommissioning in 2024.

With 2 neutrons and one proton, Tritium loses a neutron during the decay process creating beta particles which then interact with nickel parts inside the plant. Nickel since it has 30 neutrons, loses a proton and gains a neutron to become radioactive Cobalt-58, which itself experiences its own decay chain.

This is the primary explanation for the 2010 contamination incident.

Since the Linear No-Threshold (LNY) model of radiation exposure states there is 'no threshold beyond which radiation should be considered safe', KAA consequently disputes the baseline findings of SRK Consulting, and thus the drafters of the initial report commissioned by the Pebble-bed Modular Reactor Company, to determine possible impact of the demonstration unit Koeberg.

LNT is a dose-response model used to estimate stochastic health effects such as radiation-induced cancer, genetic mutations and teratogenic effects on the human body due to exposure to ionizing radiation.

The model "statistically extrapolates effects of radiation from very high doses (where they are observable) into very low doses, where no biological effects are observed" and is disputed by members of the Nuclear Industry.

The LNT model is nevertheless the foundation of a "generally-accepted postulate that all exposure to ionizing radiation is harmful, regardless of how low the dose is, and that the effect is cumulative over lifetime."

The National Nuclear Regulator currently deems anyone who accepts the LNT model, to be 'opponents of nuclear power', and thus Peter Becker was recentl,y suspended from his position on the Regular as a civil society representative by Minister Gwede Mantashe.

For the record, Koeberg Alert is opposed to the current Koeberg reactor design (including its several descendent design types, and including Nuclear 1 and the PBMR. The group is not opposed to nuclear technology in general, since it accepts that multi use reactors, (such as the proposed SAFARI-1 replacement) may in principle be necessary for medical purposes.

Its criticism in this regard is merely with regard to the management of waste fission products.

item.title: Dear South Africa
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
OUR country's measurably corrupt justice system continues to discriminate on the basis of race, culture and religion. Both the Labour Court and Labour Appeal Court have upheld the view that Judaism is a monolithic entity in which all Jews are required to practice Rabbinical Judaism and insist, that if we do not, we should not bother seeking protection from the courts for anti-Semitism meted out on the basis of offensive inquiries into religion.

Worse still, the lower courts deem it fit to define race identity, alongside religion, hold absolutely no regard for freedom of the press and press privilege, openly malign members of the Music Industry, and have sort to close down and deny rights commonly held by all South Africans, rights entrenched in our Secular 'We the People" Constitution. I note here there are other persons who have leveled similar criticism, and thus refer readers to several statements already made by Lindiwe Sisulu.

As the subject of an irregularly-gained and disputed 2010 decision handed down by an adjudicator presiding over a matter involving his own client and business partner, I once again find myself objecting to a finding which copy-pastes and interpolates the respondent's case as my own, and then proceeds to issue a determination which is clearly contrary to our secular Constitution [para 128]:

"The Applicant insists that it his prerogative to decide how to observe the Shabbat. Without deciding whether an employer is obliged to accommodate an employee’s observance of a religious practice even if the employee does not himself observe it in the manner contemplated by the religion, an employer may surely raise a question over whether the commitment to observe a religious practice is genuine."

It was Thomas Jefferson who stated: "I never will, by any word or act, bow to the shrine of intolerance or admit a right of inquiry into the religious opinions of others" and Voltaire who said of religious intolerance: "The supposed right of intolerance is absurd and barbaric. It is the right of the tiger."

Not only have the esteemed justices of our land, sort to close down my argument, and thus my objections, but they deem it fit to deny access to Legal Aid on the basis that while the respondent, a media company intimately involved in the creation of the apartheid system may level false accusations in the form of a vexatious counter-case, they are not bound by the findings of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, while I am expected to follow the rules to the letter. The thus corrupted justice system acts with impunity, behaving as if 1994 never occurred and we are still living under apartheid.

Witness paragraph 98: "His evidence is unreliable because he is engaged in a campaign against the Respondent for its support of apartheid and its refusal to apologise for doing so before the Truth and Reconciliation Commission. That is clear from his pleadings, the documents he compiled, the evidence he gave and the emotion with which he displayed in conducting his case. This is what drove him and the evidence of his personal engagement with the Respondent was shaped to advance this campaign. His evidence was tendentious."

To compound matters, I appear to live in a vacuum created by a long-standing dispute involving the legal status of the State of Israel, in which past Chief Justice Mogoeng Mogoeng has been sanctioned for his strong views on the subject, while Judge Siraj Desai is able to express an opinion providing blanket support for religious intolerance and violence, and even the removal of rights currently afforded South Africans, rights such as the rights of LGBTIQ+ persons to be recognised as persons. Iran a country whose laws he has given full support, has a death penalty for homosexuality.

Petitions to the Constitutional Court on the matter have gone unanswered (in any event I do not live anywhere near the court in terms of its rules) and it seems I am trapped inside a Byzantine and Kafkaesque system whose requirements are profoundly discriminatory against anyone not in possession of sufficient funds to procure legal representation, let alone one who does not possess the senior counsel required to argue the matter.

Nevertheless I have drafted a 70-page Affidavit, alongside an evidence bundle, setting out the manifest corruption involving labour broker and erstwhile professor of law, Halton Cheadle, whose Resolve Group was involved with Kagiso, a media company providing content at the time to Multichoice, then a division of the respondent, Media24, and whose directorship of law firm Cheadle, Thompson Haysom was explained away at a disciplinary inquiry before Cape Law Society, as having 'no bearing on the status of his client', who was the respondent at the time.

I thus once again appeal to the public to assist me in gaining access to my rights, in completing the documentation required, in bringing the perpetrators of the fraud to book, in particular as it relates to the impugned findings of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, my status as a journalist and veteran of the struggle for freedom, and the resulting breach of our Constitutional dispensation.

Kind regards

DR LEWIS

item.content:encoded:
The NEPZA is in discussions with Binance and Talent City to establish a special economic zone for bitcoin and cryptocurrencies in West Africa.

  • Nigeria seeks to create a special economic zone for bitcoin and cryptocurrencies.
  • NEPZA is in discussion with Binance and Talent City to establish a partnership.
  • The economic zone will reportedly mirror the Dubai Virtual Free Zone.

Nigeria is seeking to create the first economic free zone for bitcoin and cryptocurrency in West Africa through the Nigeria Export Processing Zones Authority (NEPZA), per a press release.

NEPZA is in discussions with Binance, one of the leading cryptocurrency exchanges, as well as Talent City which specializes in building special economic zones.

Our goal is to engender a flourishing virtual free zones to take advantage of a near trillion dollar virtual economy in blockchains and digital economy," said Adesoji Adesugba, NEPZA's managing director.

Furthermore, NEPZA explained that if a partnership is reached, the final product would mirror that of the Dubai Virtual Free Zone.

In fact, this past December, Binance entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with the Dubai World Trade Center. The memorandum intends to make Dubai a hub for bitcoin and cryptocurrency related products and services by creating a “new international virtual asset ecosystem.”

In February of last year, the Central Bank of Nigeria issued a letter banning regulated institutions from “dealing” with bitcoin or cryptocurrencies. Following the ban, Nigeria saw an uptick of 27% in peer-to-peer (P2P) bitcoin transactions across the country.

Indeed, just last year Africa as a whole became the largest country in P2P transactions in the world by volume. Around the same time, Chainalysis reported a global adoption index which showed Nigeria in the top 10 countries worldwide for its adoption of bitcoin.

Moreover, as Dubai and Nigeria look to establish special economic zones to benefit bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, we can take a look at existing economic zones. For instance, the free city of Próspera is an example of a customizable economic framework.

item.title: Life in a time of Heretics II
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
OVER THE WEEKEND IOL chose to publish a paid propaganda piece by the Republic of Iranian, to mark Quds Day, a holiday 'created by  Imam Khomeini on August 7, 1979' in which it is abundantly clear the writer views the City of Jerusalem, and the plight of Arab Palestinians, within the exclusive domain of Islam.

Instead of proposing any solutions, the piece instead pursues a clear contestation and battle over Judeo-Christian meaning within the context of a religious war, one which has its roots in the Middle Ages. The writer's solidarity with the contemporary nationalist cause of the Arab Palestinians, must be seen within the context of replacement theology, Global Jihad and a broader campaign of supersessionism, in which one party to the conflict seeks to dislodge and replace the other.

The Iranian regime itself, is currently beset by an Anti-Hijab uprising following the death of 22-year-old Mahsa Amini in police custody on September 16, 2022. This month Iranian government imposed harsher new measures to enforce women to follow the mandatory wearing of the hijab alongside plans to install surveillance cameras "across a number of public places, including highways and roadways," to identify and catch women who violate the country’s extremist dress code. 

This follows reports of the mass poisoning of schoolgirls in Iran on 30 November 2022, in the city of Qom. Targeted chemical attacks against girls’ schools have been reported in 91 schools located in 20 provinces across Iran". “The poisonings have already resulted in hundreds of schoolgirls being hospitalised." The Iranian regime continues to implement the death penalty for LGBTIQ individuals and cannot be termed an 'ally' where human rights and secular freedoms are concerned.

Attack against civilians and propagandist promotion of violence should be seen within the context of a global Jihad being waged against believers and non-believers alike in which persons outside the fold of hardline Shiite Islam are considered Infidels or Kaffirs, -- the result turns civilians into Heretics much in the way that Medieval Europe and the Spanish Inquisition turned those with which it disagreed into renegades and apostates,

Those who renounce their religion, and who are particularly at risk from the fatwas issued by the Iranian regime.

Eight months ago, on August 12, 2022, author Salmon Rushdie was attacked by a religious zealot whilst delivering a lecture on literature. The booker prize winner is the subject of a Fatwa issued by Iran's Ayatollah Khomeini calling on Muslims to 'kill Rushdie'.

Rushdie was forced into hiding for nearly a decade following the controversy over his book Satanic Verses. Iranian clerics and members of the Iranian Parliament have continued to stated that the extra-judicial death decree is valid, and various rewards have been posted including a bounty running into millions of dollars.

When 24-year-old assailant, Hadi Matar from New Jersey stabbed Rushdie on stage before he was to deliver a lecture at the Chautauqua Institution in New York it sent shock waves around the world, with world leaders and literary stalwarts saying 'they were appalled at the attack on the author who championed free speech and lived under the threat of assassination for nearly half his life'.

A similar situation played itself out during the Friday 13, Novmber 2015 Paris attacks, where a series of coordinated terrorist attacks by Islamic zealots,took place in Paris most notably the Club Bataclan, where where Islamist gunmen were involved in a mass shooting at an Eagles of Death Metal concert attended by 1,500 people in the Bataclan theatre, leading to a stand-off with police. The attackers killed 130 people including 90 at the Bataclan theatre.

At the same time, the Cape Times, instead of marking the event, chose instead to run with series promoting the campaign of a former member of the Nazi Youth Peter Plum, who at the time was suing the allies, for as he termed, it, their starting WW2. The Independent Group claimed it was publishing the pieces in order to provide a context missing from the popular discourse, that Germans were innocent victims of Hitler, and one should, add, the Jews were entirely to blame for the Holocaust.

The Quds piece is couched within terms which similar reject contemporary Judaism, alongside the existence of Israel namely, the"Zionist enemy and its religious and historical claims". A discussion on the relative merits of each parties competing claim to the Holy Land is not the purpose of this piece, rather I wish to raise some political facts which may be inconvenient, even unpalatable to some.

The exodus of Iranian Jews (namely the emigration of Persian Jews from Iran) began in the 1950s with later migration waves from the country during and after the Iranian Revolution of 1979, with the community of 80,000 dropped to less than 20,000. By most accounts, the migration of Persian Jews after the Iranian Revolution has been attributed to 'fear of religious persecution, economic hardships and insecurity'.

Although the Iranian constitution purports to respect the rights of non-Muslim minorities, the countries often virulent attacks against the West and Israel and Iran's anti-Zionist policies create an uncomfortable dilemma for many Iranian Jews. The chief of which is that Judaism itself is focused around the Holy Land in particular Jerusalem, with the city forming part of the theology.

During the Jordanian occupation of East Jerusalem (1948-1967), the Jewish quarter was destroyed, which include the Hurva synagogue and the adjacent Nachmanides synagogue, built in 1267 and also the Jewish cemetery whose tombstones were used in later constructions.

The Tifereth Israel synagogue was also destroyed alongside the ancient Beth El Yeshiva in the Old City of Jerusalem, established in 1737. Beth El was the most influential of the mystical yehivas, led by Yemeni sage Rabbi Shalom Shar’abi zt”l. More importantly Jordan destroyed the ancient Sephardic Porath Yosef Yeshiva adjacent to the Western Wall, deliberately using explosives to remove all Jewish learning from the old City, exiling hundreds of students.

As scholars note, 'This was not an attack on “Zionism”, but rather on the core of Judaism. Jews were not allowed to pray at the Western Wall in Jerusalem between 1948-1967".

Those Jews who Non-Zionism is the political stance of Jews who are "willing to help support Jewish settlement in Palestine ... but will not come on aliyah.

Minister Pandor's DIRCO has released an inflammatory statement claiming "Israel does not have the 'right to defend itself' using military means, as Israel is the occupying power" and by implication, Hamas are justified in their 7/10 massacre and daily rocketing . Yes the statement condemns the lamentable loss of civilian life inside Gaza (the toll is alarming) but it falls into atrocity denial, reaching into conspiracy theory and hyperbole, in failing to note the circumstances or the context of continued rocket attacks by Hamas, a terror organisation which currently holds over 200 hostages, and thenby providing no substantive guidance on what it expects from Israel or the World for that matter. It then proceeds to attack Zev Krengel of the SAZF, as if he is somehow the cause of the problem, in the process creating an unsustainable, false distinction on the basis of ethnicity and religion.

Yes Judaism is a religion. No, you can't remove Zionists from the picture in the Middle East by turning them into Heretics. DIRCO are threatening to investigate anyone supporting Israel's defensive military operation, and claim Krengel has libeled Minister Pandor by spreading 'false statements on the slaughter of children by Hamas'.

item.title: Legitimate resistance of theocrats?
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
WE live in a strange time, one in which the goals of the far left appear to have merged with the far right. Intersectional lefties fighting microagressions, pronouns and demanding decolonization have become vectors of ancient religious hatred, opponents of contemporary secularism, agents of old fashioned authoritarianism.

" There is a grotesque distortion of events past and present" writes Norman Lewis, a research fellow at MCC Brussels, who says the apartheid analogy " distorts the truth about the struggle against Apartheid. And it distorts the truth about Hamas by portraying it as a national liberation movement."

"The ANC Umkhonto we Sizwe was formed in 1961 under Nelson Mandela. It was a political initiative to bring the Apartheid regime to the negotiating table, rather than a serious attempt to overthrow it by force"

In a recent interview Hamas official Ghazi Hamad says the group intends to 'repeat the Oct 7 onslaught many times', in fact the event is 'just the beginning'.

Faced with an existential threat, Israel has not exactly waved an olive branch at it's adversary. The humanitarian pause over the past week in which hostages were released is not because Hamas have suddenly turned into humanitarians.

Nevertheless the release of a group of hostages from the 240 held in Gaza was used as an opportunity to present the group as 'kind gentleman' only killing those hostages that really deserve to die, releasing those lucky enought to simply be forced at gunpoint to write favorable reviews whilst singing the organizations praises.

The Bibas family were not so lucky,

The administrative detention of hundred of Palestinians by Israel is a bone of contention, displaying the extant to which the Zionist state has gone to quash successive Intifada.

Yet comparing the situation with the practice of a far cruder, detention without trial in South Africa presents a number of problems. Where Israel questionable has a judicial review process via it's military courts, no similar legal review was available to detainees imprisoned during apartheid's State of Emergency.

The objectives of the AntiApartheid struggle were also never at issue, one could always refer to our secular Freedom Charter. Allies of the movement were this never confronted with a parallel narrative, admitted Islamists repackaged as Democrats, nor were the forced to candy-coat or apologize for actions taken against the Pretoria regime

item.title: Future South Africa Positive Scenario
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
SINCE my previous posting paints a picture of a dystopia under BRICS authoritarianism, I thought I would put on rose-colored spectacles and conduct a thought experiment. What would South Africa look like if we embraced policies based upon national self-interest, evidence-based research, adopting scientifically-proven public policies that implement reasonable developmental goals?
After deciding to focus its attention on African development instead of global geo-political intrigues which characterise BRICS, our return to the African Union ushers in unprecedented innovation. The special economic zones (SEZ) have attracted a plethora of global manufacturers attracted by the concessions which include cutting red-tape. Our ports have been automated and are connected via an efficient rail network operated by several regional entities. The private rolling stock competes for shareholders attention as the countries drive for efficiency is the result of efficient capital allocation and price discovery. The days of government bureaucracy and inefficiency are over. The bottleneck which plagued most of the past decades, and which throttled services are long gone.
In their place an efficient administration has grown from the ashes of the old state. Since the introduction of a market-driven economic model, one in which taxation supports a social wage, a host of reforms have been implemented. These include jettisoning those experiments which have failed, no sense in flogging a dead horse (See here).

item.title: Talk talk must replace war war
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded: MY wish for this year is that we all spend a little more time to engage each other and our respective communities with active peacebuilding and compassionate communication aka non-violent communication. Over New Yeart I spent some time reading Marshall Rosenberg's classic 'Non-Violent Communication: A Language of Life'. I do agree with many of his ideas about developing a compassionate understanding of language interaction, focusing on people's immediate needs rather than morality and passing judgement, but of course disagree completely with what some might term, woke attempts to police so-called 'microaggressions'. Lack of compassion for others is indeed at the heart of many of our conflicts, but attributing wrong-doing to those who speak harsh words, and reaching out for legal solutions for colorful speech, accomplishes exactly what Rosenberg eschews and rejects which is to pass judgment on others. "What I want in my life is compassion, a flow between myself and others based on a mutual giving from the heart." writes Rosenberg Nevertheless his book is required reading for anyon wishing to adopt a more compassionate response to the many conflicts which have embroiled communities over the past year. I enclose a link below, and wish you all a Peaceful, Fruitful and Prosperous 2025..

item.title: Zealot’s Mirror: The Inquisition and the Global Intifada
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
IN THE annals of history, wherever faith and fury collide, the Inquisition stands as a chilling monument to ideology unleashed. Centuries later, the rallying cry to "globalize the intifada" and liberate Palestine 'From the River to the Sea' has reverberates across the world's campuses

Initially dressed up as a simple quest for Arab statehood, the global intifada in the aftermath of 'Al Aksa flood',  has taken on the unashamed character of a religious inquisition or crusade.

Yet even prior to the tragic events launched by Islamists to avenge the Yom Kippur War, the 'resistance' had already transmuted into an interrogation of secular identity.

One has merely to assess the strange cross-examination of Jewish candidate judge David Unterhalter by our JSC (nobody else's was question about international issues) or the routine targeting of academics and  individuals solely on the basis of their outlook on the issue of Palestine -- the result is a modern equivalent of  De Torqumada's  burning of 'Judaizers' , a trauma that scarred Jews and Christendom alike for generations.

The phenomena —medieval Europe’s religious purges and today’s call for a worldwide Palestinian uprising, are world's apart frm, cancellations, boycotts and calls for  sanctions that were the stock of the anti-apartheid movement.

Beneath the fervent banners, an uncanny parallel world emerges: both driven by protagonists convinced that purity, whether of religious doctrine or political cause, demands radical action and intervention into all aspects of life, prepared to take violent actions whatever the consequences.

In South Africa,which sees itself as beyond critcism due to its struggle against apartheid, even before it  launched action before the ICJ seeking to overturn history itself, Jewish communities shrink under pressure, from a peak of 100 000 to barely 40000 today.;

As Breitbart Joal Pollack put it tackled Daily Maverick Ferial Hafajee " "

in America, moderates from either camp are being drowned out by conservatives on both sides, raising the spectre of a global retreat into religious conservativism. Islamic radicals have merely unleashed Christian reactionaries opposed to birth control and worse.

In South Africa and America, this modern echo of the Inquisition’s puritanical zeal reveals a struggle not just for land or belief, but for the soul of resistance itself. And by that I mean secular resistance against tyranny,

The symmetry is even more striking. Where the Inquisition hunted heretics to preserve a Catholic order; the global intifada targets "Zionists" to uproot a perceived colonial rule, it matters not that Jewish connection to the Holy land predates both Islam and Christianity or that the Jewish people are the only people able to claim the territory was their kingdom prior to colonial rule.

Both Inquisitions wielded moral certainty — torture then, terror now—to enforce their vision. The Spanish expulsion of Jews in 1492 echoes a parallel in demands to purge Israeli influence from the Johanessberg City Counci, or the constant stream of literature seeking toto cleave Judaism between those who support the Jewish State and those who do not. While the Inquisition was based upon state edict, it's contemporary is a diffuse rebellion comprising Jihadists and their allies.

The Inquisition, launched in the 12th century by Pope Gregory IX, was the Catholic Church’s response to to he spread of heresy. Its protagonists—Dominican friars, Spanish monarchs like Ferdinand and Isabella, and later the Roman Holy Office—cast themselves as defenders of divine truth. "We must root out the weeds that choke the vineyard of the Lord," Gregory declared in 1231, setting the tone for a campaign against Cathars and Waldensians. In Spain, the Inquisition fused faith with state power, targeting conversos — Jews and Muslims forced to convert—suspected of secret apostasy. "It was about control, not just creed," says historian Henry Kamen, author of The Spanish Inquisition.

By the 17th century, the Roman Inquisition’s gaze fell on Galileo, silencing him for daring to shift the heavens. Thousands perished—some 3,000–5,000 in Spain alone—yet the architects still saw it as a sacred duty

History refracts, not repeats. The Inquisition faded into infamy; the intifada’s long arc continues with a fracturing of modernity that looks set to imperil the multitude based upon their beliefs.

item.title: PARROT MEDIA: Questioning AIDS and BIRD FLU statistics.
item.dc:creator: davidrobertlewis
item.content:encoded: JUDGING from reactions to my last posting, its a big crime in this country to question statistics of any kind. Gosh, what happens if those numbers are wrong? Some empiricists could lose their jobs while we all get into a flap about fowls dying of influenza, or mother hens keeling over from the sniffles. Imagine, if we're wrong, your budgerigar could die. Aside from not being much of a bird lover (Okay, okay, I do like pelicans and flamingos) I would rather be a dead duck than be forced to believe some bird-brained bullshit I don't believe in, which is why I am willing to fight to the last penguin standing for my freedom to speak. Call me a common tit but as far as I'm concerned, Independent Group are a bunch of parrots, repeating whatever they find on the wires and unwilling to check the facts. After being placed under discursive sanctions for questioning AIDS statistics, I was finally banned for my post-911 views on US imperialism and the war on terror. Nobody believes in the War against Terror anymore, but there are sure as hell a lot of people who believe in the Bird Flu Pandemic (50 deaths and counting). Did I forget to mention AIDS? Used to be a deadly disease until it got downgraded by the Centre for Disease Control after a scientific breakthrough in 1996. Knocked you off your perch, didn't I? PS: Aren't we all terrified about the thought of cows dying from HIV? Did anybody bother to ask them how they feel, or was the last MAD COW EPIDEMIC just another one of those newsroom decisions, one makes on the spur of the moment, and with profits in mind? PPS: Any guess as to how much is going to be spent on keeping the official death toll from BIRD FLU secret? How much is this story worth to the media in terms of bullshit and spin-doctoring? Public interest organisations that stand to make millions from scare stories about the 1918 flu disaster in a world before antibiotics and vaccines...and the hysteria continues.

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Scribble

The terrible tragedy of our time, is not the AIDS phenomenon per se (some people dying, others living, still others seemingly immune) but that our national debate has been polarised by the mass media, who basically milked the story for all it was worth, even going so far as to induce a national crisis, in an effort to dethrone MBEKI, one of South Africa's truly great individuals. The truth about AIDS is rather different from the mass hysteria generated by ignorance and media manipulation.
Yes, people need ARVs, Yes, there are problems with delivery of health care, Yes you need to wear a condom and campaign for better service, but freedom of thought is a terrible burden and not worth sacrificing. The problem with the scientific paradigm (as related by the media) is that it presumes an ability to predict the outcome of events.
If one buys into science without freedom of thought, you end up in a psychotic world, filled with hazard, a 30seconds-to-midnight paranoid schizo hell in which nothing is real, nor ever curable, and considered safe.We may be as paranoid about TB and BIRD FLU as we are about AIDS, but only those open minded enough not to swollow the lies will avoid getting caught in a knot about Birds having sex, or TB sufferers having an absolute right to anonymity and privacy. I say make AIDS a notifiable disease and settle the problem of statistical analysis once and for all.
That way, we will all sleep a lot better, knowing that the stats haven't been manipulated for political ends. That's right, what we have right now is basically the same kind of bullshit you get at a riot, with the Police downplaying numbers and rioters exagerating crowds, in the expectation something can be gained from loading the bases on either perspective.
NOTE: I AM NOT AN AIDS DENIALIST AND HAVE NEVER DENIED THE EXISTENCE OF MEDICAL SCIENCE.
Hope that sorts out the way I feel. As for that problem with Independent. After taking their word for it, I actually went looking for victims, and hospital wards overfilling with patients, only to find that most of them had been sent home with medication, and that ARVs actually worked, too my utter surprise. The story from a laymans perspective wasn't considered worthwhile investigating further, and I was subjected to verbal abuse from Judith Soal, and discursive sanctions from Cape Times assistant editors, Colin Howel and Jen Crocker, and that was just for starters.

Well, I missed the last post you mentioned but I'm right there with you on this issue.
I had reason recently to be in touch with several people in different media, mostly print, and I was amazed to see that large newspapers have moved from being journos to merely information processors - receive all the crap running on the wires, internet, whatever and pick out what's seems interesting and put in for print.
There is no judgement whatsoever. They don't even care - just fill those damn blank pages.
I'm more and more convinced that it's becoming an industry with no soul - if it hasn't already arrived.
AS for the issue of "pandemics" or threatened pandemics - my question is what are we being distracted from. LOOK EVERYONE - BIRD FLU! While we're all tranfixed we're being buggered somewhere else.
How dangerous is this? How many have died, according to media? About 100. Who gives a shit?
How many died right here in SA yesterday from crime, drugs, poverty, psychiatric drugging and other forms of abuse?
Same with the aids issue. Every time this is questioned (as it was by Mbeki some years ago) the idiots come out of hiding. How many people actually KNOW what aids is all about. Very few. Most go with whatever the mainstream says - and that's a fucking disaster.
what a good place to go to look for parrot stuff

item.title: SUPERSIZED MEDIA: Independent Group in contravention of telecommunications regulations?
item.dc:creator: davidrobertlewis
item.content:encoded:
THE Independent Group's interest in Clear Channel and other affiliates could contravene sections of South Africa's telecommunication regulations laws. The regulations implemented by the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA), the regulator of telecommunications and broadcasting sectors, sets a precedent for the limitation of media ownership and particularly the cross-ownership of media.

Clear Channel is an international radio, television and billboard company and its local affiliate, Clear Channel Independent is 40.3% owned by Independent Media PLC, the holding company of the so-called "Independent Group". The telecommunications act of 1996 contains some exciting news for would-be media barons. The no-holds barred Regulations in Respect of the Limitation of Ownership and Control of Telecommunication Services in Terms of Section 52, has this to say: "No person who holds an ownership interest or control interest in a licensee in any telecommunications service category in a concentrated market, or an affiliate of such person, shall hold an ownership interest or control interest in another licensee in the same telecommunications service category." The emphasis on alleviating pressure in concentrated markets is an important one -- the question whether a newspaper company should own a billboard company that owns radio and television stations available in South Africa, "in the same telecommunications service category" is intriguing in the absence of licencing. Newspapers are registered but not licensed. But such distinctions have been rendered meaningless in the information age. Having already crossed the boundary seperating print from electronic media, should Independent now also be allowed to enter mobile telephony as some form of service provider? There seems no end to the Independent expansion. Does the IOL/Clear Channel/Independent deal and other deals within the group contravene the act, vicariously perhaps? It's a question that media pundits are simply too afraid to answer for fear of offending CEO Gavin O'Reilly. Groundbreaking cross-media deals that blur traditional lines seperating various categories of media are the signature tune of Independent's new chief. The question is, do they contravene the laws as they stand? And if not, should our laws be updated to address problems within the sector? There is already a very real threat of an overconcentration of media in the hands of the few, without the addition of new media convergence such as internet and mobile telephony -- South Africa's mass media is owned by just a few individuals, a virtual elite, who operate without any checks and balances to prevent manipulation of public opinion and the censorship of news. Calls for an end to the Independent Media cartel are growing as increasingly the issue of supersized media is being taken up by journalism and media departments around the country. Will nothing less than a partial or total dismantling of the so-called Independent Group and restrictions on other conglomorates be needed to achieve the diversity and freedom of debate necessary in a growing democracy? The Size Issue will follow this breaking story as government moves to end the cartel that is censoring debate within the newsroom. From THE SIZE ISSUE -- A CRITICAL LOOK AT SUPERSIZED MEDIA

item.title: Koeberg Reactor Near Meltdown no cause for concern!
item.dc:creator: davidrobertlewis
item.content:encoded: YESTERDAY'S near meltdown at Koeberg, South Africa's only commercial nuclear power station resulted in a "scramble" by employees to shut the reactor down. The ensuing blackout plunged Cape Town's flatland into darkness and left thousands stranded. Traffic jams and frozen lifts were reported all over the city. The automatic shutdown caused after a warning system reported a fault inside the reactor was "no cause for concern" according to officials, and was the second time in two years that the reactor had to be shut down.In scenes reminiscent of Three Mile Island, (depicted in movies like The CHINA SYNDROME), the reactor core begun to flare out of control, before tracking rods could be inserted. Luckily the situation rectified itself after the safety mechanism scrambled allowing a general shutdown of reactor activity. Failure of such mechanisms have been blamed for both the Three Mile Island and Chernobyl disasters. At Chernobyl, engineers running an experiment were unable to shut down the reactor, and the resulting meltdown breached containment areas resulting in the devastation of the surrounding environment,loss of life of hundreds of thousands and an airborne plume of radiactive dust that reached as far as Iceland. There are currently no workable plans for evacuating Cape Town in the event of a containment breach at Koeberg. Although the Koeberg reactor has already reached the end of its productive cycle,the power station has been allowed by authorities to run for nearly a decade past its specifications. The blackout thus represents both a material and engineering breakdown. Decommissioning of such a plant is however considered too costly, as the core will be "hot" for millenia. The half-life of plutonium for example, is measured in thousands of years -- the time it takes for such material to become half as reactive. Despite warnings from interest groups such as Koeberg Alert and Earthlife Africa, Eskom continues to pursue nuclear energy as a "viable alternative to coal and gas", and has done virtually nothing to implement renewable and environmentally safe energy. With insurance at a premium, the company is unlikely to get backing from any financial institution for such a project without help from central government. Now is the time to sue Cape Town local government for protection from the threat of future disaster, not after such a disaster has happened!

item.title: Carpal Tunnel, a metaphor for our virtual world?
item.dc:creator: davidrobertlewis
item.content:encoded:
In the age of global communications, long-distance connectivity, and telepresence, could Carpal Tunnel Syndrome, that mysterious illness from the nineties be a metaphor for our time?
While many doctors swear that the Carpal Tunnel refers to a nerve in the hand, pictured above, I believe the syndrome refers to something a lot more complex than mere nerve pain. Think about it. As the human-machine interface becomes more complex, and technology begins to magnify the power of the computer user, many of us will begin to experience a "virtual hand" that operates deep within the machine, clicking away at windows and carrying out invisible operations that impact and effect the lives of millions.
The result ironically is something akin to nerve pain -- the pressure feedback, but not from a physical hand, but a more virtually magnified limb.
Often mistaken for repetative stress, Carpel Tunnel Syndrome, significes something a lot more sinister than mere pain. Where exactly is one's hand when moving a window on a virtual desktop? The mind-body, hand-eye coordination needed to achieve the miracle of modern computing has a high price.
At first there is the simple tap, and click click of the finger. Then there are the feedback loops built into professional programmes that funnel information back along the same neural paths. Virtual Impact. Over years, the brain is educated by the machine into accepting or rejecting various stimuli.
Take the neurosurgeon operating on a patient via remote telepresence. Such an event once considered a science fiction impossiblity is now an everyday occurance. Without telepresence, the force feedback of points and clicks, a wrong snip or click-cut could have both legal and moral ramifications, not to mention signifying physical disaster.
It is in this mysterious area of virtuality where South Africans are increasingly become more hooked in, more connected, or disconnnected, as more of us experience the dreaded Carpel Tunnel, that accidents like Koeberg occur.

item.title: Earthlife Africa failing to articulate anti-nuclear position in face of greenwash
item.dc:creator: davidrobertlewis
item.content:encoded: EARTHLIFE AFRICA are failing to articulate a coherent response to last week's accident at Koeberg. Despite indications of a potential class 9 nuclear emergency and radioactive accident at the plant, after the system "scrammed", the group seems to have bought into the Atomic Energy Corporation's (AEC) spin on the near-disaster. The AEC has downplayed the accident, from an all-out scram, to a minor refueling incident, to problems with an external electrical connection. If the backup and secondary systems had failed, the reactor would have been unable to switch-off, triggering a meltdown that could have disasterous consequences. Instead of examining the design flaws and possiblity of contamination within the plant structure, Earthlife has focused on the secondary "refueling incident". The term - Meltdown - refers to melting of the fuel in the reactor. According to the nucleartourist website, the term has been loosely applied to refer to any case of fuel melting, however minor. The site claims that "only in several events" such as Three Mile Island 2 and Chernobyl, " has there been significant fuel melting and only in the case of Chernobyl were there significant offsite releases." Such understatement and disinformation is to be expected from the nuclear industry. In the interests of informed debate, I republish nuclear tourist's, description of a meltdown, please bear in mind that it carries the same design-hubris that launched the failed Space Shuttle and created other technology responsible for catastrophic human errors: Overheating of the fuel typically can be caused only if there is an inability to remove heat from the fuel. Two situations are the only likely causes: * Loss of coolant in the reactor cooling system followed by a failure of the emergency core cooling systems to operate * Failure of the reactor protection system to shutdown the reactor down when required for a major fault Such conditions are considered to be outside the design basis for nuclear plants and are referred to as Class 9 accidents. The design of the plants is intended to assure that such conditions do not occur - due to the redundancy and diversity of the reactor protection, emergency core cooling, and containment isolation systems, as well as the containment structure itself. In spite of this, the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission is requiring licensees to develop procedures for such cases. The procedures are referred to as Severe Accident Guidelines. If a meltdown does occur, a release of radioactive materials to the environment can occur ONLY IF there is also a major failure of the containment structure. For this to occur, the following would also have to happen: * Overpressure of the containment * Failure of the containment isolation systems, lines, and valves to close. Potential causes of containment overpressure are: * Steam explosion in the reactor vessel or a dropping of at least 20% of the fuel mass of a molten core * Generation of gases either due to hydrogen generated from a chemical reaction between Zircaloy (used in the fuel cladding) and steam at temperatures above 3400F or due to carbon dioxide generated from interaction of molten core material with the concrete structures under the reactor. * Heating of the containment atmosphere due to a failure of the containment cooling and spray systems. For there to be a meltdown with releases offsite, the following sequence would have to occur: 1. Failure of the reactor to shutdown when required such that it continues to produce heat at a high rate OR a major amount of coolant is lost from the reactor cooling system, 2. Diverse and redundant high and low pressure emergency cooling systems are unable to provide cooling to the reactor cooling system, 3. Fuel melting starts and blockage of flow channels occurs in the reactor such that cooling cannot be provided, 4. Diverse and redundant containment cooling and spray systems are unable to provide cooling to the containment atmosphere, 5. Redundant Hydrogen recombiners will not operate, 6. Containment isolation system and associated valves do not close as required, 7. Specialized high efficiency particulate, absolute, and charcoal filters do not function as required. The design of the plant systems is intended to reduce the likelihood of such an event occurring (e.g. once in 250 years for the 400+ reactors with current designs). It is impossible to say, with 100% certainty, that a fuel melting event will not occur. The redundancy and diversity of plant design, NRC regulations, plant Technical Specifications, plant operating procedures and operator training and qualification provide the defense in depth. from http://www.nucleartourist.com/events/meltdown.htm

item.dc:creator: davidrobertlewis
item.content:encoded:

This is the only way South Africa can regain its trust and standing with a people that it massacred in defence of the indefensible.
